name: MonarchBarChart
title: BarChart
wrapsNative: Swift Charts Chart with BarMark (position(by:) for groups, yStart/yEnd for stacks), RuleMark for the zero and reference lines, RectangleMark for the inspected band, chartXSelection(value:) / chartYSelection(value:) for inspection; inside MonarchChartFrame with MonarchChartLegend and an AXChartDescriptor
summary: A bar or column chart of one or more series per category, grouped or stacked, vertical or horizontal, with value labels, a highlighted category, reference lines, touch inspection, legend toggles, drill-in and the data as a table.
whenToUse: To compare amounts across a handful of categories or periods, or to show how a few series make up each category's total.
whenNotToUse: For a ranked list of labelled values with no axis, use MonarchBarList. For a trend over many points, use a Swift Charts LineMark in MonarchChartFrame or MonarchSparkline. For parts of one whole, use MonarchDonutChart.
api: init(_ title: String, categories: [String], series: [MonarchBarChartSeries], description: String? = nil, categoryTitle: String? = nil, valueTitle: String? = nil, summary: String? = nil, orientation: MonarchBarChartOrientation = .vertical, layout: MonarchBarChartLayout = .grouped, status: MonarchChartFrameStatus = .ready, hiddenSeries: Binding<Set<String>>? = nil, highlightedIndex: Int? = nil, referenceLines: [MonarchBarChartReferenceLine] = [], valueRange: ClosedRange<Double>? = nil, showsValueLabels: Bool = false, segmentSeparator: Bool = false, isLegendToggleable: Bool = true, isTableToggleShown: Bool = true, emptyMessage: String? = nil, footer: String? = nil, height: CGFloat? = nil, labels: MonarchBarChartLabels = MonarchBarChartLabels(), formatValue: ((Double) -> String)? = nil, onRetry: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onSelect: (@MainActor (Int) -> Void)? = nil)
MonarchBarChartSeries.init(_ key: String, label: String, values: [Double?], color: MonarchChartColor? = nil)
MonarchBarChartReferenceLine.init(_ value: Double, label: String? = nil)

MonarchBarChartLabels.init(frame: MonarchChartFrameLabels = MonarchChartFrameLabels(), category: String? = nil, total: String? = nil, noData: String? = nil, details: String? = nil, clearSelection: String? = nil)

options.name: title
options.description: The chart's name: the frame heading and the plot's accessibility label.

options.name: categories
options.description: The categories in display order, already formatted by the app (dates, months, names).

options.name: series
options.description: The measures, each with a key, a label, one value per category and an optional colour slot.

options.name: description
options.description: One line under the title.

options.name: categoryTitle
options.description: The heading of the category column of the table and the name of VoiceOver's category axis.

options.name: valueTitle
options.description: What the values measure; the name of VoiceOver's value axis.

options.name: summary
options.description: Replaces the generated spoken summary.

options.name: orientation
options.description: vertical columns or horizontal bars.

options.name: layout
options.description: With several series, grouped side by side or stacked.

options.name: status
options.description: ready, loading, empty or error. Ready with no categories or no series shows empty.

options.name: hiddenSeries
options.description: The keys of hidden series. Without it the chart keeps its own set, changed by the legend.

options.name: highlightedIndex
options.description: A category to emphasise; the bars of the others are dimmed.

options.name: referenceLines
options.description: Dashed lines across the bars at a value, with an optional label.

options.name: valueRange
options.description: Fixes the value axis. Swift Charts fits the values, zero and the reference lines when nil.

options.name: showsValueLabels
options.description: Writes each bar's value at its end; a stack shows its total once.

options.name: isLegendToggleable
options.description: Whether legend entries show and hide their series. The legend appears with two or more series.

options.name: isTableToggleShown
options.description: Whether "View as table" is offered.

options.name: emptyMessage
options.description: The message of the empty state.

options.name: footer
options.description: Notes under the chart.

options.name: height
options.description: The plot height: 240 points for columns; 32 points per category, at least 120, for bars.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings, including the frame's.

options.name: formatValue
options.description: Writes values on the value axis, in value labels, the inspection row, the table and the summary. A number in the current locale by default.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Shows Try again in the error status.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Drill-in: called with the category index from Details in the inspection row or from the VoiceOver action of that category.

options.name: segmentSeparator
options.description: Sets the parts of a stacked bar apart with a thin gap, so neighbouring series stay distinct without relying on colour. Stacked layout only.

states.name: ready
states.description: The plot, the legend (two or more series) and "View as table".

states.name: inspecting
states.description: After a touch or drag on the plot: the category's band is shaded with the muted background and a row under the plot reads its values (and the stack total), with Details (when onSelect is set) and Clear. It stays until Clear or another category is touched.

states.name: highlighted
states.description: With highlightedIndex, the other categories' bars are drawn at reduced opacity.

states.name: series hidden
states.description: A hidden series is not drawn and its legend entry is struck through; the others keep their colours. The table still lists it.

states.name: table
states.description: "View as table" replaces the plot with every category and series as text, plus a Total column when stacked.

states.name: loading
states.description: The frame's muted placeholder of the plot's height, read as "Loading chart".

states.name: empty
states.description: MonarchEmptyState with "No data yet" and the empty message.

states.name: error
states.description: The frame's error, with Try again when onRetry is set.

appearance: Bars take the theme's data slots 1 to 5 in series order, then the subtle text colour. The value grid uses the subtle border colour, the zero line the strong border colour, and axis and value labels the muted text colour. Reference lines are dashed in the subtle text colour. The inspected band uses the muted background. Every colour is a theme role, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes are covered.
platformNotes: Built on Swift Charts instead of the web's hand-drawn SVG. Touch inspection uses chartXSelection / chartYSelection; the values show in a row under the plot rather than a floating tooltip, so they are never clipped and wrap at large text sizes. There is no keyboard arrow navigation; VoiceOver gets the chart descriptor (Audio Graphs) and one action per category for drill-in instead. Categories are strings the app has formatted (the web formats dates and numbers itself). Series have no dashed style: Swift Charts bars cannot be outlined with a dash; use the neutral colour slot for a comparison series. hiddenSeries is a Binding (controlled) or internal state, not separate default and change callbacks. The inspected category is internal, not a controlled activeIndex. Android ships the same MonarchBarChart. Several closures are optional (formatValue, onRetry, onSelect). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is formatValue.
accessibility: The plot is one accessibility element labelled with the title. Its value is the generated summary (number and range of categories, each shown series' total and highest category, each reference line) or the summary parameter.

The plot carries an AXChartDescriptor built from the table: a categorical axis of the categories, a numeric axis named by valueTitle, and one series per table column with the app's formatted values, for Audio Graphs and the chart data rotor.
With onSelect, the plot has one VoiceOver custom action per category, named "Details, <category>".
The inspection row is ordinary text followed by MonarchButton controls with 44-point targets.
The legend is MonarchChartLegend: each entry is a switch that is on while its series is shown; the last visible series cannot be hidden.
"View as table" shows every value as text; each table row is read as the category, then each series and its value.
Series are told apart by the legend's names and the table, not by colour alone; a highlighted category is also reported by nothing but opacity, so the highlight is decorative.
edgeCases: Gaps (nil) and values that are not finite draw no bar, are written "No value" in the inspection row and "–" in the table, and are left out of the summary and the chart descriptor.
Negative values draw below (or before) the zero line; in a stack they stack down from zero separately from the positive values, and the stack's label shows the net total at the end with its sign.
Categories with the same text are one category to Swift Charts; give each a distinct label.
More than five series: the sixth and later are neutral, as in the legend.
Long category names in horizontal bars wrap or are truncated by Swift Charts' axis; the full names are in the table and the inspection row.
A highlightedIndex outside the categories dims every bar.
chartXSelection and Audio Graphs were not tried on a device or with VoiceOver; the descriptor, summary, inspection text and action names are unit-tested.

examples.title: Grouped columns
examples.template:
MonarchBarChart(
    {{title}},
    categories: [{{categories.0}}, {{categories.1}}, {{categories.2}}, {{categories.3}}, {{categories.4}}, {{categories.5}}],
    series: [
        MonarchBarChartSeries({{series.0.key}}, label: {{series.0.label}}, values: [{{series.0.values.0}}, {{series.0.values.1}}, {{series.0.values.2}}, {{series.0.values.3}}, {{series.0.values.4}}, {{series.0.values.5}}]),
        MonarchBarChartSeries({{series.1.key}}, label: {{series.1.label}}, values: [{{series.1.values.0}}, {{series.1.values.1}}, {{series.1.values.2}}, {{series.1.values.3}}, {{series.1.values.4}}, {{series.1.values.5}}]),
    ],
    description: {{description}},
    categoryTitle: {{categoryLabel}}
)
.environment(\.locale, Locale(identifier: {{locale}}))
examples.code:
MonarchBarChart(
    "Posts",
    categories: ["Week 1", "Week 2", "Week 3", "Week 4", "Week 5", "Week 6"],
    series: [
        MonarchBarChartSeries("drafted", label: "Drafted", values: [12, 9, 15, 11, 14, 18]),
        MonarchBarChartSeries("posted", label: "Posted", values: [8, 9, 11, 10, 13, 12]),
    ],
    description: "Drafted and posted per week",
    categoryTitle: "Week"
)
.environment(\.locale, Locale(identifier: "en-US"))

examples.title: Stacked horizontal bars with totals, legend bound to the app, drill-in
examples.code:
MonarchBarChart(
    "Tickets by team",
    categories: teams,
    series: [
        MonarchBarChartSeries("open", label: "Open", values: [42, 18, 27]),
        MonarchBarChartSeries("closed", label: "Closed", values: [120, 64, 88]),
    ],
    categoryTitle: "Team",
    orientation: .horizontal,
    layout: .stacked,
    hiddenSeries: $hidden,
    showsValueLabels: true,
    onSelect: { opened = teams[$0] }
)

examples.title: One series with the current month highlighted
examples.code:
MonarchBarChart(
    "Signups",
    categories: ["Apr", "May", "Jun"],
    series: [MonarchBarChartSeries("signups", label: "Signups", values: [52, 47, 60])],
    highlightedIndex: 2,
    height: 160
)
